# Charlotta

## Overview

- **Age:** Fifteen years old  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c16 P12](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0012), [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive, married  <sub>[v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038), [v4 c3 P40](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0040)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper, maid-of-all-work  <sub>[v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Charlotta the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>; Charlotta the Fifth  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>

## Appearance

Charlotta the Fourth is a girl with a very freckled face, a wide mouth, a snub nose, and a cheerful, wide grin. She wears her fair hair in long braids tied with extraordinarily large blue ribbon bows, which she later gives up in favor of an enormous pompadour as she grows older. Though she is not considered conventionally pretty, she is known for her vibrant expressions, energetic movements, and blue eyes.

_Sources: [v1 c16 P12](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0012), [v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c28 P27](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0027), [v2 c28 P39](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0039), [v2 c29 P1](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0001), [v2 c29 P8](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0008)_

## Personality

Charlotta is immensely energetic, dutiful, and intensely loyal to her employer, Miss Lavendar. She possesses a brisk, cheerful demeanor and a very practical mind, though she is easily captivated by romantic ideals. She idolizes Anne Shirley and strives to emulate her grace, speech, and mannerisms. She is outspoken, highly affectionate, and approaches her duties with passionate efficiency.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c28 P27](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0027), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055), [v2 c29 P4](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0004)_

## History

Born as Leonora Bowman, she entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge at age thirteen. Because three of her older sisters had previously worked there, Miss Lavendar affectionately dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta greeted them and assisted Miss Lavendar in entertaining them. Charlotta came to idolize Anne, attempting to mimic her carriage, gestures, and way of speaking. She managed the household at Echo Lodge with fierce devotion, constantly keeping things orderly and protecting her mistress from loneliness or discomfort. When Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta eagerly supported their romance and helped prepare for their wedding. Following Miss Lavendar's marriage to Stephen Irving, Charlotta moved with them to Boston to continue her service. While in Boston, she married an American bricklayer named Tom, though she retained her fiercely patriotic devotion to Prince Edward Island.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P12](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0012), [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c28 P12](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0012), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071), [v2 c29 P3](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0003), [v2 c29 P4](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0004), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033), [v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038), [v4 c3 P40](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0040)_

## Background by volume

- Her real name is Leonora Bowman, but she is nicknamed Charlotta the Fourth by Miss Lavendar because her three older sisters preceded her in the same household role.  <sub>[v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- She went to work for Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge at the age of thirteen.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- She married a man named Tom, a bricklayer from Boston.  <sub>[v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038), [v4 c3 P40](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0040)</sub>

## Quotes

> Courting’s all right in its place, Miss Shirley, ma’am, but if you try to mix it up with cooking and scouring everything’s spoiled.  <sub>[v2 c28 P12](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0012)</sub>

> You’ve just got to hope for the best and prepare for the worst and take whatever God sends.  <sub>[v2 c28 P16](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0016)</sub>

> A wedding ain’t much cheerfuller than a funeral after all, when it’s all over, Miss Shirley, ma’am.  <sub>[v2 c28 P35](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0035)</sub>

> When all’s said and done, Miss Shirley, ma’am, there’s many a worse thing than a husband.  <sub>[v2 c28 P76](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0076)</sub>

> I don’t want no Yankee accent. Not that I’ve a word to say against the Yankees, Miss Shirley, ma’am. They’re real civilized. But give me old P.E. Island every time.  <sub>[v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010)</sub>
